channel.title: Nature Materials
channel.description: Nature Materials is a multidisciplinary journal aimed at bringing together cutting-edge research across the entire spectrum of materials science and technology. Nature Materials covers all applied and fundamental aspects of the synthesis/processing, structure/composition, properties and performance of materials. Nature Materials provides a forum for the development of a common identity among materials scientists while encouraging researchers to cross established subdisciplinary lines. To achieve this, Nature Materials takes an interdisciplinary, integrated and balanced approach to all areas of materials research while fostering the exchange of ideas between scientists involved in different communities.

item.title: [7] Excitons in van der Waals magnetic materials
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Xiaodong Xu, Vinod M. Menon

Authors: Pratap Chandra Adak, Florian Dirnberger, Swagata Acharya, Akashdeep Kamra, Xiaodong Xu, Vinod M. Menon

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant review of vdW magnetic semiconductors and light-matter interactions in 2D systems.

Tags: #review #vdWmaterials #magnetism

Abstract: Nature Materials, Published online: 03 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02636-0 In this Review, the interplay of excitons, magnons and photons in two-dimensional magnetic semiconductors and how this enables control of light–matter interactions are discussed, and promising opportunities for magneto-optic optoelectronic and quantum applications are surveyed.

item.title: [8] Fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect in moiré fractional Chern insulators
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Jian Xie, Xiaobo Lu

Authors: Tingxin Li, Jianpeng Liu, Jian Xie, Xiaobo Lu

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: High-impact perspective on anomalous Hall and topological states in moiré materials.

Tags: #moiré #FQAHE #topological

Abstract: Nature Materials, Published online: 03 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02649-9 The fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect serves as the defining experimental manifestation of fractional Chern insulators at zero magnetic field. This Perspective surveys its realization in moiré materials, examines underlying mechanisms and outlines pathways towards new fractional and non-Abelian topological states.

item.title: [8] High-Chern-number orbital magnetism in twisted rhombohedral graphene
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Cyprian Lewandowski, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero

Authors: Xirui Wang, L. Antonio Benítez, Skandaprasad Rao, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of topological magnetism and Chern numbers in twisted graphene systems.

Tags: #graphene #magnetotransport #Chernnumber

Abstract: Nature Materials, Published online: 03 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02659-7 Magnetotransport measurements and mean-field calculations of twisted monolayer–multilayer (1 + n) rhombohedral graphene reveals high-Chern-number orbital magnetism with Chern number C = n. Electrical and magnetic switching of these states is also demonstrated.
